# Small local transcript-cleanup evaluation evidence

These public snapshots record actual small-model runs and their source/artifact pins.
**They do not establish a Windows whole-app SLA pass or a final production model selection.**
The requested 15% allowance is 747,500,000 bytes of whole-app host memory and 805 ms
from release to complete text. Cleanup-only timings, Linux working sets and synthetic
or public-audio replays do not alone establish those two application limits.

The collection preserves exact copied bytes. [The SHA-256 index](evidence-files-sha256.json)
covers every file here except itself. [The collection catalog](collection-manifest.json)
records original work paths, stages and terminal states. Absolute paths inside reports
are historical provenance from this execution workspace, not promises that those paths
exist on a reader's machine.

## Completed native stages

| Stage | Completed runs | Terminal failed attempts | Output rows |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `screen` | 14 | 0 | 336 |
| `resource-native` | 21 | 0 | 315 |

| `mmap-native` | 2 | 6 | 10 |

`screen` compares 14 prompt/model conditions using 13 downloaded model artifacts;
Handy's two renderer conditions are separate. `resource-native` changes resource
settings in a labeled sequence. `masked-development` records the earlier literal
protocol; `masked-v2-development` uses the compact specialist protocol. They are
native replays of Core-normalized development inputs, not physical Windows dictation.
[Manual reviews](reviews) record semantic judgments and their scope; structural/automated
checks alone do not establish fidelity. [The quality protocol](quality-protocol.md)
describes grading and separation of development from held-out evaluation.

`speculation-native` records the tested prompt-lookup conditions. `mmap-native`
and `loadmode-native`, when present, keep their exact flags and runtime configuration.
The initial six `--no-mmap` attempts are retained under
[diagnostics](diagnostics/mmap-initial-invalid-cli) as native CLI compatibility failures.
They contain no no-mmap inference measurements and provide no model-quality judgment.
A terminal failed attempt remains a failure; its missing cases are not successes.

## Text, resource and actual-ASR scope

[Production prompt exports](prompts), [compact-mask exports](masked-v2-prompts)
and [public ASR text exports](actual-asr-text-prompts) preserve the exact input conditions.
The underlying development text is public synthetic text. Actual speech replay uses
public JFK-derived material; no private recordings or microphone capture are included.
The [committed synthetic held-out corpus](fixtures/frozen-holdout.json) is archived only
after the initial frozen qualification, with its prior SHA commitment preserved.
[Frozen Core reports](frozen-core) separate model candidates, accepted/fallback text and
delivery counts. Later [GPU-candidate quality validation](gpu-candidate-validation) uses
that already consumed corpus and is labeled post-holdout evidence, not a new blind test
or evidence of GPU execution. [Final development runs](final-development) retain the
v3 restoration and prompt-lookup comparisons before qualification.

[Actual ASR replay reports](actual-asr) include production-pinned Parakeet CPU speech
recognition, Core orchestration and optional cleanup under their recorded Linux profiles.
Their simultaneous process working-set sums exclude the desktop UI and can double-count
shared pages. Reports distinguish warmup/load and release-to-complete trials; small,
repeated public-audio samples do not establish a field latency distribution or accuracy
on ordinary users. A counting injector does not type into a foreground application.
The [final frozen closed-loop summary](final-closed-loop/summary.json), raw cohort reports,
run plan and post-run verification retain GC ramps, CPU/memory attribution and exact
executed-file/source hashes. Those 25 Linux partial-pipeline trials do not establish a
Windows whole-app pass; neither tested CPU candidate passed both partial limits.
[Windows qualification](windows-qualification.md) records the remaining platform scope.

[Observer/configuration controls](actual-asr/observer-controls) retain both raw replay reports
and the derived [memory analysis](actual-asr/observer-controls/analysis.json). The original
control reports predate a global aggregation fix, so their global/trial peaks can differ.
Use the conservative maximum observed **simultaneous** process snapshot across both windows;
do not sum independent component maxima. Raw values remain unchanged for audit. These are
Linux research overrides; the production speech runtime configuration was not changed.

## Provenance and the local ScribeKey conversion

[Artifact/source metadata](metadata) records immutable download revisions, exact complete
file hashes and native-library inventory. Model download size is not runtime memory.
Prepared manifests reference local artifacts by absolute path and hash. Source/assembly
freezes identify the implementation used by a stage; raw reports are not rewritten when
later source changes. Source bodies and binaries remain outside this evidence collection.

[Conversion evidence](conversion) records original verified BF16 weights converted with
pinned b12015 tools to F16 and then Q4_K_M. It is a locally derived research artifact,
not a publisher-produced Q4 download. Original tensor names/dimensions, architecture,
vocabulary and special tokens were audited. Compatibility-only tokenizer wrapper changes,
full metadata differences, inherited license/source notices and exact tool/dependency pins
are recorded. No Q8 GGUF was used as conversion input, and no calibration or pruning ran.
The metadata audit also corrects an intermediate startup concern: trace logging guards
skip its example formatter under `--log-disable`; no required startup change was inferred
from that trace statement. Actual native launch belongs to its separate run evidence.

A verified local prepared manifest can address the derived Q4 file. Settings acquisition
needs a separately authorized immutable hosted copy of those exact derived bytes and
notices, or a separately implemented local-conversion flow. The original safetensors/Q8
URLs cannot substitute for a Q4 download. Nothing in this collection was published or
uploaded to a model host.

## Verified Windows Vulkan preparation

[Windows Vulkan metadata](metadata/windows-vulkan) records the official same-version
b12015 archive's full SHA verification, safe extraction, complete DLL/notice inventory
and two prepared model bundles. No Windows executable or GPU ran during those checks.
The static device-selection audit uses an exact discovered NVIDIA `VulkanN` backend
name through process-scoped `LLAMA_ARG_DEVICE`; it does not translate logical names
into physical-device filter ordinals. Synthetic parser checks are labeled as such.
GPU and CPU-on-Vulkan templates use fresh isolated copies; CPU control explicitly
uses zero GPU layers and device `none`. Driver availability, real selected-backend
offload, per-PID GPU telemetry and full target-app qualification remain untested here.

[Final source validation](verification/source-validation-summary.json) retains the exact
successful logs proving 585 .NET tests across four projects, 112 regular Pester tests
and 57 Python tests. Published Linux self-test, Windows cross-publish/static PE and
[verified preview ZIP metadata](windows-preview) retain their separate scopes. Source
launcher/helper snapshots are text only; no preview executable/model/archive is tracked.
Cross-publishing changes RID/build metadata and compiled hashes; it does not establish
byte identity with Linux performance assemblies or execute Windows behavior.

## Collection boundaries

Full weights, safetensors, runtime/managed binaries, Torch packages/wheels, raw publisher
pages, private audio and general build logs are excluded. Model legal documents are referenced
by immutable URLs and byte hashes rather than reproduced wholesale; the short pinned
MIT runtime source license accompanies its authored source audit. Tiny meaningful
native CLI diagnostics are retained with their failed-attempt reports.

The repeatable collector is `work/cleanup-small-models-2026-11-03/collect_public_evidence.py`
in the original workspace. It copies only completed/terminal public stages, refuses to
overwrite differing finished snapshots and writes the evidence hash index last. The optional
`--append-revision PHASE` preserves a reviewed changed source under a distinct revision path;
it never replaces the original snapshot. Later
stages and final verification may be appended with distinct paths; regenerate the index
after any append. Other authored protocol/qualification documents are preserved.
